clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old woman from Sumba tribe, Indonesia, with 10-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (on oral medication) and hypertension (BP 140/95 mmHg) presented for routine six-month check-up. She reported incidental symptoms of weakness and dizziness. Initial physical examination was otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory workup revealed a Mentzer Index <13 and peripheral blood smear showing hypochromic microcytic anisopoikilocytosis with ovalocytes and target cells, prompting further investigation for hemoglobinopathy. Hemoglobin electrophoresis confirmed homozygote HbE with HbE 89.4%, HbA 2.9%, HbF 3.8%, and HbA2 3.9%, explaining the microcytic anemia and presenting symptoms. The final diagnosis also includes renal complications, attributed to long-standing diabetes and/or hypertension in the context of this patient's 10-year disease history.
